title: Queue-row measure pass and draw pass disagree when amber_pct == 0 (counter guards amber_pct > 0, draw loop does not)
detail: With amber 0 the counter counts only queued pipes (test pins this), but u32(0) makes the draw's util_pct < 0 check never true, so every queueless pipe draws a row. Measure and draw diverge row-for-row; the pipes path guards red<=0 in both places.
recommended_fix: Mirror the pipes pattern in the queue draw: `if amber_pct <= 0 { if q==0 { continue } } else if q==0 && util < amber { continue }`, and pin a measure-vs-draw agreement test at amber 0.

title: Spec added in this diff promises line_rate_bytes_per_tick; PR body in the same diff says it was removed as dead, and units.odin never defines it
evidence:
spec: "`transit_ticks(pb, cap)`, `line_rate_bps(pb, cap, hz)`,
     `line_rate_bytes_per_tick(...)` (= frame_bytes/transit — the honest
     reference)," — PR body: "N8 `line_rate_bytes_per_tick` removed (dead);"
detail: Two files added in the same diff contradict each other about a symbol that does not exist in core/units.odin. The spec's design section is stale relative to the r2 fold it ships alongside.
recommended_fix: Strike `line_rate_bytes_per_tick(...)` from the spec's units.odin design list (or annotate it removed per r1 N8) so the shipped spec matches the shipped code.

title: node_health comment example keeps the "util" prefix the new format string no longer prints
evidence:
comment: `// throughput as a real rate (the unit canon — same derivation as the
// pipes). "util 150% (load 1.5 KiB / 33 Mbps)" — a 🔴 node stays` — code: `trace := fmt.tprintf("%d%% (load %s / %s)", pct, pp.format_bytes(load_bytes), node_rate)`
detail: The comment's example output reads "util 150% (load ...)" but the format string is "%d%% (load %s / %s)" — no "util" token is emitted. The comment misquotes its own code.
recommended_fix: Update the comment example to "150% (load 1.5 KiB / 33 Mbps)" (the PR body table already uses the prefix-free form).

title: bundle_tx_window lacks the defensive ring-length check that bundle_tx_record has
detail: Record tolerates an undersized ring; window indexes base+s unchecked and would panic in the identical scenario (e.g., n advanced without rebuild). The defensive posture is applied in one proc and dropped in its sibling.
recommended_fix: Add the same `base + UTIL_WINDOW_TICKS > len(b.tx_slot_tick)` guard (return 0) to bundle_tx_window, or drop both guards and document the rebuild invariant in one place.

title: Tick 0 collides with the ring's "never written" sentinel — a tick-0 record writes a slot the window can never count
detail: At tick 0, tx_slot_tick[s] stays 0 (0 == 0, no re-key), and the window's `st > lo` (lo=0) excludes st==0 forever, so tick-0 served units are silently uncountable. Safe only if production's first stepped tick is 1 — an assumption the diff never states.
recommended_fix: Key slots with tick+1 (or a written bool), or assert/comment the tick>=1 contract at bundle_tx_record so the sentinel collision is impossible by construction.

title: Select-readout row-count comment still says "offered + carried" after those rows were replaced by rate/tx
detail: The offered/carried lines were swapped for rate/util and tx/q/dropped lines, but the measure-pass comment enumerating the four rows was not updated. Count is still 4; only the label went stale.
recommended_fix: Rephrase the comment to "section + rate + tx/q + drops" so the row-for-row contract stays self-documenting.
